# Importing your bank's CSV export

Ledger can read the CSV file your bank lets you download and add its transactions to your ledger.

## 1. Download the export from your bank

Sign in to your bank's website and download your statement or transaction history as a CSV file. Note where it was saved, for example `~/Downloads/statement.csv`.

## 2. Run the import

From your Ledger folder, run `bun run import` with the path to the file:

```sh
bun run import ~/Downloads/statement.csv
```

Ledger adds each new transaction to `ledger.csv`.

## Importing the same file again

You can safely import a file more than once, or import exports with overlapping dates. Ledger skips transactions it has already imported, so they won't be added twice.

## Troubleshooting

### The file is too large

Ledger refuses files over 10 MB. Split the export by month, then import each part:

```sh
bun run import ~/Downloads/statement-2026-08.csv
bun run import ~/Downloads/statement-2026-09.csv
```

Many banks let you choose a date range when you download the export, so you can download one month at a time.

### Ledger says columns are missing

Banks name their CSV columns differently. If Ledger reports missing columns, it doesn't recognize your bank's column names, so you need to add a column mapping for your bank's export in `ledger.config.json`. Then run the import again.
